s: a state of relative luxury, ample sufficiency, especially with regard to mod cons
Komfort.et: 19th century, partly from English comfort (hence the -m-), partly from French confort (hence the mute -t), both from Old French confort, from conforter, from Latin confortare.

s: well appointed, especially with mod cons; relatively luxurious, amply sufficient
komfortabel.et: 19th century, from English comfortable and French confortable. Equivalent to Komfort + -abel.
